name: Erase structure

guide.summary: Remove stones, walls and porous beads.
guide.biology: Opening a barrier lets microbes and dissolved food that were kept apart mix again.
guide.rules: Each covered cell with a stone, wall or porous bead gets back the water, gel or sediment it had before the structure was placed. A bead keeps what it held; a stone or wall cell held nothing and starts empty. The rim is never erased. Erasing is an ordinary undo point. No material is made or lost.
guide.example: Erase one stone from a line between two groups and watch them meet.

where: Cells with a stone, wall or porous bead (other cells are left alone; the rim is never erased).
dose: Removes the structure from each covered cell.
changes: Only the structures: the water, gel or sediment underneath is exactly as it was before.
doesNotChange: Nothing is added. A freed stone or wall cell starts empty and fills by ordinary spreading.
watchFor: Organisms and food moving through the opening.
